Forget using 32bit wine which ships with most repositories. Compile from source.
Why would you want to have 64bit wine when in the most cases you still gonna run 32bit apps?
Most software today is 64bit and the ia64 instruction set is backwards compatible. Now you don't need to install multilib.

You don't. Keep your prefixes separate, and install different versions of Wine for each application, depending on its needs. This is the standard approach, due to the intricacies and differencess among the various Wine development versions. So, install a 64-bit Wine version and use that to run your 64-bit app, and install a 32-bit Wine version to run your 32-bit app. PlayOnLinux gives you a great GUI to help you manage all of this, as well as juggling all the repositories you need to make everything work.
